summary: Microburst heartbeat mismatch causing slot starvation and autoscale lag in dedicated pool
description: Issue summary: Customer reports repeated throughput dips and p99 latency spikes in their dedicated pool during two 20–30 minute windows daily. Impact: ParcelFlow.ai is observing increased inference errors and tail latency causing user-facing timeouts in their shipment-tracking webhooks (3–5% request failure, p99 increased from ~220ms to ~1.8s). Environment: Dedicated pool (region: us-west), reserved GPUs (A10x8 pool), mixed short and medium-length streams. Steps to reproduce: 1) Run load test using 120 concurrent short streams (keepalive) plus periodic medium-length requests. 2) Observe allocator_attach and slot utilization. 3) Notice steady CPU and KV cache metrics while allocation credits drop and batches stop forming. Observed behavior: During the windows, the allocator's attach rate drops, GPU slot leasing stalls for ~10–40s, and autoscaler enters a cooldown/inhibited state despite queued requests. Metrics show a burst of short-lived connection heartbeats misaligned with the allocator heartbeat, followed by a mini-wave of background I/O from a tenant-side logging sidecar. Expected behavior: Stable attach rate, autoscaler reacting within configured thresholds, minimal p99 variance. Logs/metrics referenced: - allocator_attach_rate (grafana/dedicated/us-west) - slot_leased_count, attach_latency_hist - autoscaler_decision_log - kernel scheduling traces (excerpt attached in comments). Additional context: Customer recently rolled out a client library version that increased keepalive frequency on short streams on their side; rollout coincides with regression start time.

investigation_notes: Collected kernel scheduling traces for affected GPUs between 2026-03-12 03:00 and 2026-03-13 04:00 UTC; saw repeated microbursts of small epoll wakeups tied to customer connector ip addresses.

Autoscaler telemetry during windows showed stable token_utilization but rising attach_latency (p95->p99). Autoscaler did not scale because the aggregated capacity metric used did not include attach_latency as a signal.

KV cache hit rates unchanged; memory pressure normal. Not a model memory issue. NVMe io_wait spikes align with sidecar log flush windows from the noisy tenant.
Hypothesis: noisy tenant sidecar I/O plus high keepalive churn lengthens attach and fragments slot batches, starving batch formation and causing autoscaler to underreact.
Reproduced locally in staging by running 200 short keepalive streams (8s) plus a small background sidecar logwriter that flushes every 25s; observed same slot-leasing stalls and batch fragmentation.
root_cause: Combination of (1) customer-sidekeepers using aggressive keepalive (8s) increasing short-stream churn, and (2) background logging sidecar I/O from the same tenant producing periodic NVMe/io-wait spikes. These together elongate attach latency and fragment batch formation. The autoscaler decision heuristic did not incorporate attach_latency, so it failed to scale despite queued demand.
resolution: Temporary workaround: customer increased keepalive from 8s -> 30s which reduced churn and removed p99 spikes. Engineering will deploy a multi-part mitigation: autoscaler sensor change to include attach_latency signal (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/1298), allocator reservation TTL backoff under high-churn mode, and scheduler IO backpressure guard to deprioritize snapshotter/sidecar IO when attach_latency exceeds threshold. Scheduled rollout: canary 2026-03-18, global 2026-03-20. Updated support runbook with recommended client keepalive defaults.
next_steps: (Engineering) Land autoscaler PR and allocator TTL change; target canary 2026-03-18.
